archetype.name: Game Manager (volume short passer)
archetype.definition: A veteran bridge starter who lives on short and intermediate throws to his tight end, avoids sacks, and is asked to throw close to 40 times a game because his defense keeps putting him behind.

report.headline: A competent short-area passer whose deep game, third downs and supporting cast are collapsing
report.take:
Brissett is what he has been for most of a decade: a big, sturdy pocket quarterback who keeps the offense on schedule, takes few sacks and rarely moves the needle by himself. His career efficiency has swung with the offense around him, from 0.111 EPA per play in Cleveland in 2022 to -0.151 in New England in 2024, and this year sits in the lower-middle at -0.075 per dropback, 33rd of 49. The yardage looks fine at 214.9 a game, but that comes from volume (38.1 attempts a game) behind a defense ranked dead last against the pass. Per attempt he is 42nd of 49 at 5.64 yards, down 1.3 from last season.

The season is split by depth of throw. Between 10 and 19 air yards he has been very good: 0.509 EPA per attempt, 29.5 EPA in total, 56.9% completions on throws that move the chains. Everything around that window has hurt him. The screen and swing game behind the line has cost 17.1 EPA. The deep ball has been close to unplayable: 19.4% completions, -17.6 CPOE, no touchdowns and three of his seven interceptions on 31 attempts. His aggressiveness is up to 23.61% from 16.5% last year, and those throws into tight windows are where the turnovers have come from, not the sacks he has always avoided.

The context flatters the totals. When trailing by nine or more he has added 15.5 EPA with a 5.4 CPOE. Within one score he has cost 40.1 EPA with six interceptions, and on 28 close fourth-quarter plays he is at -0.625 per play. Third down is the worst of it: 30.1% conversions, five interceptions and -41.3 EPA, a long average distance (7.3 yards) that a short-throwing passer struggles to convert. The red zone has produced 10 touchdowns despite -0.277 EPA per play, which points to sneaks and short-field scores rather than sharp passing. One split stands out the other way: under center he has 7 touchdowns and no interceptions, while all seven picks came from shotgun.

The outlook has got worse since the start of October. Over his last three games he is at -0.178 EPA per dropback with one touchdown pass, and in Week 8 Dallas pressured him on 58.6% of dropbacks before he left having played 58% of snaps. He sat out Week 9 without practicing. Now Gardner Minshew's elbow puts him back in as QB1, but Michael Wilson (74 targets) is out for the season, Kendrick Bourne is on IR, the center is in concussion protocol, and a guard and a tackle are out. He returns to a thinner offense than the one he struggled with.

strengths.title: Intermediate window is legitimately good
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards have been the engine of the offense: 0.509 EPA per attempt with a positive CPOE. This is the seam and dig area where Trey McBride works, and it fits Brissett's whole career as a timing passer. It should hold up, but it depends heavily on McBride now that two of the other three main receivers are gone.

strengths.title: Avoids sacks under pressure
strengths.body: He turns only 22.4% of pressures into sacks, 11th of 42, and his sack rate is below the league average. He has ranked near the top in this area before (9th in 2019, 12th in 2022), so it is a lasting trait rather than a fluke. It matters more now with three linemen on the injury report.

strengths.title: Sneaks and under-center offense work
strengths.body: His 17 designed runs have an 82.4% success rate on 1.71 yards a carry, which is the profile of a 235-pound quarterback converting sneaks. Under center he has 7 touchdowns and no interceptions. The offense is at its best when it is compact and physical, not when he is dropping back on obvious passing downs.

concerns.title: Third downs and close games
concerns.body: On third down he converts 30.1% and has cost 41.3 EPA with five interceptions. Within one score he is at -40.1 EPA total, while his best numbers come when trailing big. This is a real limit: a passer without a deep game can't convert third-and-long against defenses that sit on the sticks.

concerns.title: The deep ball is a turnover source
concerns.body: He completes 19.4% of throws of 20-plus air yards, at -17.6 CPOE, with three interceptions on 31 attempts. The rise in aggressiveness from last year has made it worse rather than opening the field. With Wilson and Bourne gone, the outside receivers he could take shots to are fewer and weaker.

concerns.title: Gutted supporting cast, uncertain health
concerns.body: Wilson, his second-most targeted receiver, is out for the season and Bourne is on IR. The center is questionable with a concussion, and a guard and a tackle are out. Brissett himself didn't practice in Week 9 after leaving Week 8 early, and the dossier doesn't say why. The recent slide has come before these losses have even fully hit.

trend.note: Weeks 1, 3 and 5 were positive-EPA games, but from Week 4 on he is at -0.174 per dropback, with one touchdown pass in his last three games. It ended with a 10-for-23 day in Dallas under a 58.6% pressure rate before he left.

nextGame.headline: Rams' stingy pass defense meets a depleted Arizona offense
nextGame.body:
The Rams rank 4th in defensive EPA and 2nd against deep passes, which shuts down the part of Brissett's game that already fails. They are also 6th against short throws and hold top tight ends to -0.07 EPA a target, the matchup that matters most when McBride is nearly all he has left. The one opening is that they barely get home: 31st in hit rate and 29th in sack rate. In Week 6 he threw from a clean pocket (17.1% pressured, no sacks, 2.39-second release), managed a small positive EPA and won 18-16 as a 12.5-point underdog.

Availability cuts both ways. Los Angeles is missing both starting corners, Trent McDuffie (out) and Jaylen Watson (IR), which should help on intermediate throws outside. Puka Nacua is doubtful, which could keep this low-scoring and take away the shootout volume Brissett usually gets from Arizona's 32nd-ranked pass defense. On his side, Wilson and Bourne are gone, the center is in protocol, and a guard and tackle are out. The Book has the Rams by 9.5 with a 40.5 total, which means a game script heavy on dropbacks while trailing but few points.

keyMatchups.title: McBride vs Rams tight-end coverage
keyMatchups.body: McBride is the only main target with strong efficiency, and the Rams are among the best in the league against TE1s by both fantasy output and EPA. If they take him away, Brissett's targets are Jalen Brooks and Tyler Allgeier, both negative by EPA per target this year.

keyMatchups.title: Weak Rams rush vs patched line
keyMatchups.body: The Rams rarely hit or sack the quarterback, which offsets some of Arizona's line losses and suits Brissett's habit of taking few sacks. The line was overwhelmed in Dallas, so whether a makeshift interior holds up even against a light rush is the key question.

keyMatchups.title: Backup corners vs the intermediate game
keyMatchups.body: With McDuffie out and Watson on IR, the Rams' outside coverage is thinner than in Week 6. That is where Brissett's 10-19-yard strength could find room, though their deep defense should still force him to throw underneath.

nextGame.watch: Whether the offense gets him to the 10-19-yard window on early downs, or leaves him in third-and-long against a defense that takes away everything deep.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect volume without efficiency. Arizona's pass defense ranks last, so he will keep throwing in the mid-to-high 30s most weeks, and the sack avoidance and sneak game are durable traits. His red-zone touchdown count has outrun his red-zone efficiency, and the receiving corps behind McBride is now weaker than what produced a -0.178 EPA per dropback over his last three games. I'd project roughly 185 to 230 passing yards a game, a touchdown pass a game or slightly less, and an interception rate that stays high while he keeps throwing tight-window shots.

The ceiling games will come in shootouts against weak defenses, like Weeks 3 and 5. The floor is games like Seattle and Dallas, when pressure gets home and there is no outlet beyond the tight end. His health is the unknown: he missed Week 9 for reasons the dossier doesn't give, and with Minshew likely done the job is his for as long as he can play.
swingFactors: His own health after missing Week 9
Center Froholdt's return and the state of the line
Who becomes the second target behind McBride

confidence.note: Unexplained absence, two top receivers lost, three linemen hurt
